stemMd: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

options.label: A
options.textMd: It follows a technology from its invention through to the range of uses it has since found in dry regions around the world.

options.label: B
options.textMd: It introduces a method, reports what its designer expected, and then explains why the results overturned that expectation.

options.label: C
options.textMd: It sets out a long-running scientific debate about a method, summarises each side's evidence, and then takes the side of one camp.

options.label: D
options.textMd: It lists several ways of supplying water to dry coastal regions and then ranks them by the cost of installing and maintaining each.

explanationMd:
Structure questions are answered by the shape of the text, not by its subject. Label each sentence with the job it does and the shape appears.

Sentences one and two set up the site and describe the method: mesh nets, gutter, tank. Sentence three gives Belmont's starting expectation and her reason for it, that a denser mesh would intercept more droplets. Sentence four reports the opposite outcome. Sentences five and six explain the mechanism behind that outcome and give the coarse mesh's better result. Method, expectation, reversal and explanation of the reversal is the option that names a method, the designer's opening expectation and the results that overturned it.

Check by testing each option against a feature the text would have to contain. A debate needs two named positions, a ranking by cost needs costs, and a history needs dates and a spread of users. None of the three appears anywhere in the passage.

distractorRationale.c: No debate is described. Only one researcher appears, no side's evidence is summarised, and the disagreement in the passage is between Belmont's own expectation and her own results, not between two camps of scientists.
distractorRationale.d: Only one water-supply method is described, and the passage mentions no prices, budgets, installation or maintenance costs of any kind, so nothing in it is ranked by cost.
distractorRationale.a: The passage gives no invention date, no history and no other users. It reports one researcher's nets on one ridge, not a technology's spread through dry regions around the world.

accessibilityText: Using the passage about Nadia Belmont's fog-collecting nets, choose the description that best matches the passage's overall organisation. The four choices say the text: follows a technology from its invention through to the range of uses it has since found in dry regions around the world; introduces a method, reports what its designer expected, and then explains why the results overturned that expectation; sets out a long-running scientific debate about a method, summarises each side's evidence, and then takes the side of one camp; or lists several ways of supplying water to dry coastal regions and then ranks them by the cost of installing and maintaining each.

provenance.notes: Original item. Each distractor names a structure that would require a feature the passage demonstrably lacks (a second position, costs, a timeline).

review.author: digital-sat-wave4-author

independentSolve.workingNotes: The passage introduces the method (mesh nets), gives Belmont's expectation (a denser mesh intercepts more), and then explains that the fine nets did worst because air could not pass. The coarser mesh did better. That matches B. [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-wave7-sat-rw-run1) reached the same answer: The text introduces the nets, gives Belmont's reasoning that a denser mesh would catch more, and then explains why that was wrong: the air could not pass through. There is no history of uses (A), no debate (C) and no cost ranking (D).]

review.notes: Author's own solve and uniqueness check: Sentence-by-sentence: method, designer's expectation and reason, contrary result, mechanism and better result. That is D exactly. A needs two positions, B needs costs, C needs a timeline and worldwide use; none is in the text. Not published: awaiting a blind independent solve by a second party. Options were reordered after review to remove answer-position bias; ids and labels were remapped with the key. v2: choices rebalanced so the key no longer stands out by length, detail or hedging (answer-length cue found by tmp/cue-scan.mjs); stem, passage and key unchanged; re-solved blind.
